note: Fixtures for detect_silent_catch (road-to-deterministic-defect-detectors 3.1). Positives are shapes the diff ADDS; negatives are either a handled error or the same silent catch present only as CONTEXT, which is pre-existing debt this check does not own.

fixtures.why: The catch block has no statements at all; the failure disappears with no trace.
A comment saying `intentional` is the one-token evasion the risk register names. Comments are not statements and do not rescue the block.
Same shape written on one line. A matcher that only reads multi-line blocks would miss the tersest spelling.
Brace-language catch with a typed exception and an empty body.
A bare except whose only statement is pass — the canonical Python spelling.

The roadmap's Risk 3 as a fixture: a trailing `# intentional` comment on the pass. The first implementation of this detector was defeated by exactly this line, so the fixture is the regression pin, not a hypothetical.
The error is bound and then never used, logged, or re-raised; the caller sees null and cannot tell absent from broken.
The error reaches a log. If this fires, the log predicate is not being read.
The error is wrapped and re-thrown. If this fires, the rethrow predicate is not being read.
The error is returned in a typed result. If this fires, the check demands a throw where a value is equally explicit.
Logged and chained. If this fires, Python handling is being read as swallowing.
The empty catch is CONTEXT, not an added line — pre-existing debt this check does not own. This is the scope negative: if it fires, the check has silently become a whole-tree sweep.
